scoring_justification: Recompute surface state energy consistency from layer DOS CSV and compare to paper gold; audit oxygen gap DOS from CSV.

hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: Sec. IV, Fig. 5 and Table I: Ti-derived surface state D1 at Γ at 2.85 eV relative to VB top.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Derived from paper: gap is 3.0 eV, Ec=3.0 eV, Ti state is 0.15 eV below Ec, so 2.85 eV.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: This is the paper-reported value for the main quantity.

hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper's claim that no occupied oxygen-derived states are present in the gap; from visual inspection of Fig. 5, any oxygen DOS in gap is negligible. We set a tight threshold to enforce absence.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Chosen to be small enough that any non-zero oxygen projection in gap would fail, but with a small tolerance for numerical noise.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: It implements the paper's structural claim that the gap is free of O-derived states.

schema.description: A single floating‑point number, energy in eV, on one line.

outputs.description: Energy of the Ti‑d surface bound state at Γ for TiO₂(110) Model I, relative to the valence‑band top.

columns.orbital: str (x2‑y2, xz, yz, xy, 3z2‑r2, x, y, z)

outputs.description: Orbital‑resolved density of states at Γ for the top three layers of TiO₂(110) Model I. The checker uses this to audit the absence of oxygen‑derived states in the gap.

output_contract.notes: The surface state energy is compared to the paper‑reported value with a hidden tolerance. The layer‑resolved DOS is audited for negligible oxygen projection in the energy interval [0, 3] eV (the band gap).

steps.description: Check Ti-d surface state energy at Γ against paper gold and consistency with Ti DOS peak from CSV.
Verify that oxygen-projected DOS in the gap is negligible.
